scope: Independent source and evidence review of the WebMCP native contract repair, including assigned-tab routing, authorization, registration lifecycle, truthful failures, and sibling procedures. No tests, build, browser, release, database, or deployment actions were run.

verified_contract: Chrome documents document.modelContext, asynchronous registerTool and getTools, executeTool with a discovered RegisteredTool and object input, execute callback registration, and AbortSignal registration removal.
Chrome documents toolchange, same-origin discovery by default, and cross-origin access requiring both fromOrigins and explicit exposedTo configuration.
The overview identifies Chrome 149 as the origin-trial starting point and the local testing flag; it does not establish native behavior for the installed browser in this task.

verdict_a_intended_behavior_and_runtime_.verdict: SOURCE CONTRACT ACCEPTED WITH ONE ROUTING CONCERN; NATIVE RUNTIME UNVERIFIED

evidence.finding: The revised availability, listing, and invocation handlers use document.modelContext, await getTools, find by tool name, and call executeTool with the discovered object and an object input.
evidence.assessment: Matches the current documented imperative API. All three handlers call getAssignedTabId(ctx), so normal agent calls preserve the assigned tab and refuse when the assigned tab has closed.

evidence.finding: Registration uses the execute callback, awaits registerTool, gives each registration an AbortSignal, aborts a prior same-name registration on re-registration, and removes registrations added by a failed pass.
evidence.assessment: Matches documented registration and lifecycle behavior. Discovery, registration, and execution rejections surface as failures instead of successful counts/results.

evidence.finding: Strict source-boundary fixtures are clearly described as mocked API evidence; the builder report expressly says no native Chrome 149+ object or execution was observed.
evidence.assessment: The source GREEN is not misrepresented as native acceptance. D150 should stay open until a receipt-bound supported-browser run.

evidence.finding: The extension-side registered tool callback loses the originating page's tab identity before dispatch.
evidence.assessment: The WebMCP message receiver has sender.tab.id available but passes neither it nor a tab-bound context to handleWebmcpCall. That function sets assignedTabId to null. Handlers using getAssignedTabId then fall back to whichever tab is active when they run, so a tool registered in tab A may target tab B after a switch. This is a source-supported routing risk, not a browser-reproduced result.

verdict_a_intended_behavior_and_runtime_.runtime_limit: No native browser version, enabled API object, discovery result, or execution result was observed. Chromium 141 installation provenance does not establish the running browser version or native support.

verdict_b_quality_and_doctrine.verdict: REPAIR QUALITY IS SOUND AT THE NATIVE BOUNDARY; FOLLOW-UP REQUIRED FOR ROUTING AND PROCEDURE ACCURACY

evidence.finding: External dispatch retains execution-time admin and schema gates, optional Chrome permission checks, action confirmation, and refuses ask-user/privileged tiers.
evidence.assessment: The WebMCP registration surface does not bypass these dispatcher protections. Action-tier external calls still require confirmation even when the user's own agent default is Act.

evidence.finding: The newly added native procedure covers discovery, invocation, page reload/re-registration, invalid and unknown input, missing API, rejected registration, and a second-tab routing check.
evidence.assessment: Useful acceptance plan, but the second-tab case is material because the extension-side bridge currently drops sender.tab.id as noted above.

evidence.finding: Earlier feature-test procedures still describe obsolete callTool and claim that WebMCP action calls run without approval in Act mode.
evidence.assessment: These instructions contradict the current native API and the external-caller confirmation policy, which can mislead manual verification. The newly added procedure does not remove the conflicting older steps.

verdict_b_quality_and_doctrine.source_fixture_boundary: The test fixture invokes the production injected function with a controlled document.modelContext shape. It is a source contract check, not native-browser proof, and the report accurately labels it.

required_follow_up: Carry the originating sender.tab.id into the extension-side WebMCP dispatch context, or explicitly bind the handler operation to the registered page tab, so tab switches cannot retarget it.
Update or retire the conflicting feature-test instructions that still call navigator.modelContext.callTool and promise no confirmation for external actions in Act mode.
Keep D150 open until discovery, invocation, and extension-side registration are exercised on an observed supported browser build with the API enabled and exact extension artifact recorded.
limitations: Source-only review; no test, build, browser, release, database, or deploy commands were run.
The origin-tab targeting concern is a direct source-path inference; no live tab-switch scenario was executed.
